Backend API Reference¶

Reference for the FastAPI backend (backend/app/main.py, routers in backend/app/routers/). This page covers authentication and the conventions shared by every route; each area of the API has its own page, listed below.

Auth¶

X-Visivo-Token: <token>          # almost every request
X-Visivo-Session: <session_id>  # dataset-scoped requests

Most routes require the X-Visivo-Token header; a missing or wrong token is answered 401. The exceptions:

Route

Access

GET /v1/ping

Always open

GET /v1/node/status, GET /v1/metrics

Open by default; require the token when VISIVO_NODE_STATUS_PUBLIC=0

GET /soda/capabilities, GET /soda/availability

Open

GET /v1/samp/files/{token}

Open (the file token is the credential)

WebSocket /v1/render/{session_id}/ws

Token in the token query parameter or the header; a bad token closes the socket with code 1008

A few server-wide routes (/v1/sessions, /v1/diagnostics/events, the listing, download and deletion of Workspace Exports, and SAMP) need the operator token once several per-user tokens are configured: the primary token, VISIVO_TOKEN. With a single token everyone is the operator.

The token is taken from VISIVO_TOKEN; when it is unset the backend generates one at startup and writes it to ~/.visivo_token, where BackendClient::readTokenFile() reads it. VISIVO_TOKENS adds per-user tokens (comma- or space-separated).

X-Visivo-Session names the backend session that holds the caller’s open datasets. Get one with POST /v1/sessions/new (or take the session_id returned by an open call) and send it on every dataset-scoped request. With a single token an absent header falls back to a shared anonymous session; with several tokens the header is mandatory (400 without it) and a session is visible only to the token that created it (404 for any other).

Error convention¶

Most endpoints return { "valid": false, "error": "<message>" } on failure. HTTP status is then typically 200 even for logical errors, and the client checks valid. Many routes also use HTTP status codes for refusals (404 unknown dataset or session, 422 unusable input, 429 no free compute slot, 503 missing optional component, 504 heavy-task timeout); each page says which. A path outside the allowed data roots is answered as 404 Path not found., the same as a missing one. An unexpected exception is a 500 with {error, error_code: "internal_error", request_id}, the id also in the X-Request-ID header.

Worker pool and heavy-task throttle¶

CPU-bound work runs in a single process pool of VISIVO_WORKERS (default 4) workers. To keep the GUI responsive while a long compute is running, endpoints are classified into two tiers:

Tier

Helper

Examples

Interactive

_run / _run_with_limit

/v1/cube/preview, /slice, /subvolume, /noise, /image/*

Heavy

_run_heavy / _run_heavy_with_limit

/v1/products/moment, /products/isosurface, /v1/cube/pv, /v1/spectral/*

Heavy invocations are gated by a global asyncio.Semaphore (_HEAVY_SEM) with capacity VISIVO_HEAVY_SLOTS (default max(1, VISIVO_WORKERS-1)), so the pool is never fully saturated by long jobs and an interactive request (slice scroll, ROI subvolume, probe) always finds a free worker.

Configuration¶

The variables that matter when calling the API:

Variable

Default

Effect

VISIVO_TOKEN

generated at startup

The primary (operator) token

VISIVO_TOKENS

(unset)

Additional per-user tokens, comma- or space-separated; enables multi-user mode

VISIVO_NODE_STATUS_PUBLIC

1

0 makes /v1/node/status and /v1/metrics require the token

VISIVO_WORKERS

4

Size of the worker pool

Every other variable (heavy slots and timeouts, moment streaming and Dask, rendering, remote-service allowlists, limits) is documented in the Configuration reference.
